blocks.text: Module 1 prepares sandbox execution reports for subsequent analysis in TemporalKG. Its implementation, LoaderFilter, discovers existing CAPE JSON reports, associates them with malware-family labels, extracts selected behavioral evidence, and exports traceable report collections. Collection in this module therefore refers to ingesting and selecting previously generated sandbox reports. The tool reads report files without executing malware samples. Its central distinction is between a report identified as a loader candidate through metadata and a report satisfying the implemented conditions for observed loader execution. [S1, S5]
a) Input data and processing scope

The input contract comprises local report directories, a loader-family taxonomy, and optional AVClass, CAPE, and consensus label mappings. Each input directory has a configured identifier and path. The supplied Volume 3 and Volume 4 configurations reference WinMET directories and external mapping files. The report adapter reads CAPE structures including target.file, behavior.processes, behavior.processtree, behavior.enhanced, detections, signatures, CAPE.payloads, dropped, and procdump. These fields provide sample metadata, process context, API-call records, and information about extracted or dropped artifacts when available. [S2, S4]

Processing separates two operating modes. The labels mode constructs the inventory and label-based selections while leaving execution decisions as not_evaluated. The evidence mode additionally parses reports and evaluates behavioral evidence. Its scope can be restricted to candidates or extended to all discovered reports. Under candidate-only processing, reports outside the initial candidate set do not undergo evidence scanning; the selection scope therefore determines the coverage of behavioral screening. [S1]
b) Source discovery and identity resolution

Discovery applies configurable inclusion and exclusion patterns, with JSON files selected in the supplied configurations. The directory traversal skips symbolic links and Windows reparse points, excludes output locations, and detects repeated references to the same physical file using its device and inode identifiers. Alternative locators are retained, and the discovered files are sorted by input identifier and relative path. An optional source-count limit is recorded as limited coverage. [S2]

Three identifiers preserve distinct levels of provenance. The source_id is derived from the input identifier and relative path; the report_id is the SHA-256 digest of the report's bytes; and sample_sha256 identifies the analyzed binary from a valid hash in the filename and/or report target metadata. This separation prevents a report checksum from being mistaken for the malware sample's hash. Content-based report identifiers also allow multiple source locations to refer to the same report content. [S1, S2, S4]

Sample identity is recorded with an explicit status. Agreement between filename and target hashes produces filename_target_agree. A filename hash alone remains filename_unverified, a target hash alone produces target_only, and missing hashes produce unresolved. If both hashes exist but disagree, the resolved sample hash is cleared and the identity is marked conflict. Evidence-mode processing checks the parsed target hash against the filename hash and preserves this conflict for subsequent decisions. [S1, S2]
c) Label reconciliation and candidate selection

The inventory joins sample identifiers to AVClass and CAPE label observations and reconciles these observations with the consensus index. A consensus entry can supplement an absent mapping; disagreement with an existing mapping is retained with its provenance rather than silently replacing the original label. Invalid label rows can be quarantined according to configuration. Label normalization removes surrounding whitespace and applies case folding, followed by explicit taxonomy aliases. The bundled seed taxonomy contains eight canonical families: smokeloader, guloader, sload, gcleaner, upatre, modiloader, privateloader, and customerloader. [S3]

A source becomes a seed candidate when at least one relevant label resolves to a seed family. The broader candidate set also includes configured generic or review labels and conflicts between label mappings and the consensus index. The inventory records whether labels agree, differ, are missing, or contain source conflicts. Seed-family membership remains provisional family evidence. Reports outside the seed taxonomy remain unreviewed rather than becoming confirmed non-loader samples. When the scope is all, evidence scanning can also add candidates based on report detections or delivery-related behavior. [S1, S3, S5]
d) Streaming extraction and evidence provenance

The CAPE adapter uses ijson to process reports incrementally. Process and API-call arrays are handled item by item, while selected unused subtrees are skipped. The adapter counts API calls and constructs process summaries containing process and parent identifiers, process names, module paths, command lines, first-seen values, and API/category counts. Detailed facts are generated for a predefined set of API names covering process creation, remote-thread and APC operations, memory operations, file operations, network activity, and handle management. Consequently, the fact collection is a targeted evidence representation, not a complete copy of the report's API-call stream. [S4]

Extracted call facts retain available timestamps, API names, return values, status values, process/call indices, and JSON pointers locating the original records. Evidence identifiers are re-keyed within each report, and related artifact records are added for CAPE payloads, dropped files, and process dumps. The resulting report.json, facts.jsonl, and processes.jsonl files retain metadata, selected evidence, and process summaries respectively. Coverage flags distinguish report regions containing data from empty or absent regions, while quality flags record problems such as missing call results or ambiguous arguments. [S4]

Resource controls bound report size, individual call-record size, nesting depth, and parsing time; worker processes support concurrent report parsing. Malformed JSON, duplicate keys, unsupported structures, resource-limit violations, and source changes are recorded as processing failures. The parser also compares file size and modification time before and after reading and computes a SHA-256 digest of the report bytes. These controls preserve the distinction between successfully screened reports and reports whose contents could not be reliably processed. [S1, S4]
e) Conservative execution decisions

The conservative-v1 policy evaluates family support, object-to-process bindings, and runtime evidence separately. Ordinary label matches provide provisional family identity. Supported family identity requires matching trusted identity rules. Automatic associations based on artifact or process metadata remain weak bindings; only trusted or reviewed bindings with a process index qualify as trustworthy. Human review can supply validated bindings and event scopes, but it does not replace the policy's family-support and execution requirements. [S5]

For the machine decision loader_run_observed, the implementation requires a trustworthy binding of the target sample to a process, supported family identity, runtime execution evidence for that process, and no invalidating identity or report conflict. Its runtime predicate requires that the process contain recorded API calls and that a successful process_create or remote_thread fact identify its PID as the target. Missing target identity, conflicting sample hashes, or insufficient support prevent a positive observed decision. Cases with relevant but incomplete evidence are routed to needs_review; screened_no_loader_evidence records the absence of qualifying evidence under the implemented policy. [S5]

Payload execution is tracked separately from loader execution and additionally requires an observed bound object other than the target sample, such as a CAPE payload, dropped artifact, or process dump. Event attribution is also separate from report selection. In event export, validated reviewed intervals determine loader or payload attribution; calls without a matching interval, or with conflicting interval roles, remain mixed_or_unresolved. Selecting a loader-related report therefore does not establish that every event in the report belongs to the loader. [S5, S7]
f) Outputs and quality assurance

An evidence-mode run retains a SQLite state database, configuration and taxonomy snapshots, input fingerprints, decision records, evidence files for successfully parsed reports, and manifests. The manifests include all_sources.csv, seed_candidates.csv, candidates.csv, observed.csv, payload_execution.csv, review_queue.csv, and all_reports.jsonl. Resume processing checks the semantic configuration and analysis fingerprint, and evidence-mode processing rechecks previously completed source content. These records connect a selection decision to its input report, labels, extracted evidence, and processing configuration. [S1, S6]

The report collection passed to Module 2 uses the candidates selection. Inclusion therefore requires candidate status and does not require the stricter loader_run_observed decision. This collection includes seed-family matches and additional candidate reasons, preserving reports that require further analysis. The export metadata records the selection rule. The available selections are distinguished below. [S7]

rows: Sources marked as seed candidates through taxonomy-linked labels.
Sources marked as candidates, including seed and additional review reasons.
Sources whose effective decision is loader_run_observed.
Sources associated with an observed-loader report whose payload_execution flag is true.

blocks.text: The reports format copies selected original JSON reports, verifies their SHA-256 values, and writes a manifest and checksums. This preserves the original telemetry for subsequent normalization and transition construction. Optional grouping by year derives the directory from available execution-related timestamps and uses an unknown directory when a year cannot be resolved. The alternative events format rereads raw calls and exports records with report/process/call identifiers, source pointers, attribution information, and associated evidence. [S7]

The pipeline implements 15 quality checks, QC-01 through QC-15, covering configuration and input fingerprints, identifier consistency, evidence-file integrity, observed-decision prerequisites, manifest counts, output structure, error reporting, and processing statuses. A separate verification command checks stored run artifacts and optional exports. These checks assess internal consistency and traceability; they do not constitute a measurement of malware-detection accuracy. Module 1 supplies selected reports and their provenance, while the subsequent Transition Builder performs telemetry normalization and constructs timestamped behavioral transitions. [S6, S8]
